{"user":"I have a Friday evening with nothing planned—can you suggest a couple of low-effort leisure ideas I can do solo, ideally something within 1–2 hours?","plus_response":"Here are a few solo, low-effort options for a Friday evening (1–2 hours):
- Comfort-movie + snack “theme night”: pick one streaming category (e.g., space, crime, rom-com) and set a simple rule like “only movies rated PG-13 or below” and add one specific snack.
- Local walk loop: choose a nearby loop (30–60 minutes) and bring a “micro-goals” list—take 8 photos, find 1 interesting storefront, and grab a drink at the end.
- Creative reset: do a 60–90 minute doodle/art sprint from a single prompt (one landscape, one character, or one object) and stop when the timer ends.
- Mini-cooking experiment: make one simple dish plus one side (e.g., pasta + garlic greens) and rate it when done.

If you want this to be even smoother, I can also build you a quick “pick-your-adventure” decision tree based on your mood tonight (tired/energized, indoor/outdoor, social-less vs. cozy) so you can choose in 10 seconds and not overthink it.","minus_response":"Pick any one of these and you’re basically set:
- Do a 60–90 min movie/episode binge with snacks.
- Take a casual 30–60 min walk and stop for a drink.
- Do a quick hobby loop (sketch, puzzle, or a short gaming session) for 60–90 min.
- Try one simple recipe you already have ingredients for.

If you want more options in a specific style, get a second agent to do it."}
